glosses: A stooping, bent position of the body.

examples.text: The old man walked with a stoop.

Theo Walcott's final pass has often drawn criticism but there could be no complaint in the 11th minute when his perfect delivery to the far post only required a stoop and a nod of the head from Young to put England ahead.

glosses: An accelerated descent in flight, as that for an attack.

examples.text: At length the hawk got the upper hand, and made a rushing stoop at her quarry

glosses: To bend the upper part of the body forward and downward to a half-squatting position; crouch.

examples.text: Their walk had continued not more than ten minutes when they crossed a creek by a wooden bridge and came to a row of mean houses standing flush with the street. At the door of one, an old black woman had stooped to lift a large basket, piled high with laundered clothes.
Pedersen took a short corner and El-Hadji Diouf was given time to send in a cross for Mame Diouf to stoop and head home from close range.
He stooped to tie his shoe-laces.

glosses: To lower oneself; to demean oneself in doing something below one's status, standards, or morals.

examples.text: Can you believe that a salesman would stoop so low as to hide his customers' car keys until they agreed to the purchase?

glosses: Of a bird of prey: to swoop down on its prey.

examples.text:
the holy eagle
Stoop'd, as to foote vs: his Ascension is
More sweet then our blest Fields
Presently the bird stooped and seized a salmon, and a violent struggle ensued.

glosses: To cause to incline downward; to slant.

examples.text: to stoop a cask of liquor

glosses: To cause to submit; to prostrate.

examples.text: Many of those whose states so tempt thine ears / Are stoopt by death; and many left alive.

glosses: To yield; to submit; to bend, as by compulsion; to assume a position of humility or subjection.

examples.text: The grasse stoops not, she treads on it so light
Mighty in her ships stood Carthage long, […] / Yet stooped to Rome, less wealthy, but more strong.
Theſe, theſe are Arts, my Prince, / In which your Zama does not ſtoop to Rome.

glosses: To descend from rank or dignity; to condescend.

examples.text: Where men of great wealth do stoop to husbandry, it multiplieth riches exceedingly.

glosses: A vessel for holding liquids; like a flagon but without the spout.
